social_history.tobacco: Former smoker 20 pack-years, quit 10 years ago
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two adult children

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache during sexual intercourse, vomiting, neck stiffness
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Thompson is a 58-year-old African American man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes who presents via EMS after his wife called 911 when he collapsed during sexual intercourse. He developed an instantaneous, catastrophic headache described as an explosion inside his head, rated 10/10 at onset. He immediately vomited twice and became transiently confused for about one minute. His wife observed no seizure-like activity. He regained full alertness within minutes but complained of persistent severe headache and neck stiffness. Paramedics found him alert but in severe distress, with a blood pressure of 196/112 on scene. He has never experienced a headache of this severity previously. He takes his blood pressure medications regularly and his last primary care visit three months ago showed BP 138/86 on lisinopril. His HbA1c was 7.4% at the last visit. He denies any prior headache disorder, vision changes, focal weakness, or hearing problems. Coital headache has been reported as a classic trigger for aneurysmal SAH and the presentation is entirely characteristic of this diagnosis.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; severe headache; photophobic
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm; EOM intact; no papilledema; no CN deficit
neurological_exam.additional: Marked nuchal rigidity; Kernig positive; Brudzinski positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.location: Basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures
findings.description: Thick hyperdense blood throughout basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures

ct.impression: 1. Subarachnoid hemorrhage, Fisher grade 3, with thick hyperdense blood throughout the basal cisterns, bilateral Sylvian fissures, and suprasellar cistern. 2. No intraventricular extension. 3. No hydrocephalus. CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 15.2 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 186 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.22 ng/mL (H), BNP 198 pg/mL (H), Lactate 2.8 mmol/L (H), HbA1c 7.4 % (H).

ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia, rate 102. Deep T-wave inversions in V1–V5. QTc prolonged at 494 ms. No ST-segment elevation. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 6.2 x 5.4 mm with lobulated morphology and daughter sac - consistent with ruptured aneurysm

output.impression: 1. Saccular aneurysm of the right posterior communicating artery, measuring 6.2 x 5.4 mm, with lobulated morphology and a daughter sac. 2. No additional intracranial aneurysms. Findings are consistent with the source of subarachnoid hemorrhage. Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning

interactions: Lisinopril + nimodipine: additive hypotension - ACE inhibitor + calcium channel blocker
warnings: Hold lisinopril during nimodipine course to prevent excessive hypotension
Monitor BP before each nimodipine dose; hold if SBP <100
Resume lisinopril after nimodipine course completion

output.wall_motion: Apical and mid-ventricular hypokinesis with basal hyperkinesis - classic Takotsubo
output.impression: 1. Left ventricular ejection fraction 44%, mildly reduced. 2. Apical and mid-ventricular hypokinesis with basal hyperkinesis — Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy pattern. 3. Mitral and aortic valves are normal. Consider repeat echocardiogram in 4–6 weeks to assess recovery of systolic function. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Consider repeat echocardiogram in 4–6 weeks to assess recovery of systolic function

output.impression: Mild right MCA vasospasm. Right MCA mean flow velocity 118 cm/s, Lindegaard ratio 3.1. Right ACA, left MCA, and basilar velocities within normal limits. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: AHA SAH management guidelines aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage 2023 nimodipine vasospasm

results.finding: Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days Class I Level A for vasospasm prevention
Aneurysm treatment within 24-48 hours to prevent rebleeding
Coital-triggered SAH has same prognosis as other triggers
Induced hypertension for symptomatic vasospasm; euvolemia for all patients

output.summary: Oral nimodipine (60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days) is a Class I, Level A recommendation for all patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, based on reduction in poor outcomes attributable to delayed cerebral ischemia. Early aneurysm treatment within 24–48 hours is recommended to reduce rebleeding risk. Transcranial Doppler monitoring is used for vasospasm surveillance following SAH. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: No clear ictal activity. Right temporal sharply contoured transients warrant continued monitoring. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from right posterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CT shows subarachnoid blood; CTA shows aneurysm - this is not benign exertional headache
Subarachnoid blood on CT; aneurysm on CTA; SAH pattern not HTN alone
CTA shows saccular aneurysm not arterial beading; CSF bloody

critical_actions: CTA identifies right PComA aneurysm - treat within 24 hours
Hold metformin if contrast given and monitor renal function
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue lisinopril with nimodipine without BP monitoring
Do not fluid restrict - risk of DCI
key_reasoning_points: Coital/Valsalva triggers are classic presentations of aneurysmal SAH
Right PComA aneurysm is one of the most common aneurysm locations
Fisher grade 3 predicts moderate-high vasospasm risk - nimodipine essential
Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) must be held - additive hypotension with nimodipine
Moderate Takotsubo EF 44% - avoid negative inotropes, needs cardiology follow-up
QTc 494 ms requires monitoring - avoid QT-prolonging agents
